group_recommendations.rationale: Both tools form a read-only search-then-retrieve pair over Twilio/SendGrid/Segment documentation and public API operation metadata; neither tool calls a live Twilio API or sends any message, so they share identical low-risk, read-only characteristics and are always used together (retrieve consumes ids returned by search).

Both tools are simple single-field, read-only natural-language queries into Wolfram's computational knowledge base (one direct query, one semantic-search context lookup), with no code execution and openWorldHint=false, making them low-risk, search/calculator-shaped tools.

Isolated into its own cluster because it is the only tool among the five that evaluates arbitrary code in a live kernel and is flagged openWorldHint=true, giving it a broader and qualitatively different capability surface than the fixed-field query tools even though it remains read-only and non-destructive per upstream annotations.

tools.description: Search Twilio documentation and API operations by natural language query. Use source="docs" for conceptual guides and setup questions, source="api" for finding specific API endpoints and operations, or source="all" (default) when unsure. Returns ranked documentation snippets and/or API operation summaries. Use twilio__retrieve with an id from API results to get full parameter schemas.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default 5, max 10. Increase only when you need broader coverage.

product.description: Optional. Restrict API results to a specific Twilio product. Only applies when source="api" or source="all". Use "api_v2010" for the core Twilio communications REST API (calls, SMS/MMS, phone numbers, conferences, recordings).

query.description: Natural language question or description of what you want to do. Be specific — 'how to set up ConversationRelay' or 'send an SMS message' work better than 'relay' or 'messaging'.

source.description: Use "docs" for conceptual guides, tutorials, and setup questions. Use "api" for finding specific API endpoints, operations, and parameters — preferred for coding tasks. Use "all" when unsure (default). "all" fires both searches in parallel and interleaves results by rank.

topics.description:
Optional. Restrict doc search to specific sources. Omit to search twilio_docs (default) when you don't know. Only applies when source="docs" or source="all".
- twilio_docs: API references, error codes, TwiML, SDK docs, tutorials (twilio.com/docs)
- support_docs: troubleshooting and account support (help.twilio.com)
- twilio_com: Twilio marketing and product pages
- twilio_customers: customer stories and case studies
- twilio_org: Twilio.org social impact content
- sendgrid: SendGrid product documentation
- sendgrid_support: SendGrid support articles
- segment: Segment CDP documentation

version.description: Optional. Omit for latest version only, "any" for any version, or a specific version e.g. "v2". Requires product to also be set when pinning to a specific version.

tools.name: twilio-docs__twilio__search
tools.risk_rationale: Upstream advertises readOnlyHint=true and destructiveHint=false. The tool only performs a natural-language search over Twilio/SendGrid/Segment documentation and public API operation metadata and returns ranked snippets; its input schema contains only query, filter and pagination-style fields (query, source, product, topics, version, limit), with no parameters that write, send, or otherwise mutate any resource.

tools.description: Fetch full parameter schemas and response details for one or more Twilio API operations or documentation articles. Use this after twilio__search to get the complete request body fields, path/query parameters, response schema, and curator guidance needed to actually call the API. Pass the id values exactly as returned by twilio__search.

fields.description: Optional. Limit which top-level fields are returned for each result to reduce payload size. Omit to receive the full spec. For API operations, 'request_body' returns request parameters and body schema; 'response_fields' returns the response schema. Identity fields (api, method, path, operation_id) are always included. All other fields — including intent, summary, description, product, version, and response_schema — are excluded when fields is set. Use twilio__search first to get intent and summary; only use fields here when you need the raw parameter or response schema.

ids.description: One or more id values (format: 'op::{api}::{operation_id}') copied verbatim from twilio__search results — do not construct or guess IDs. Only call this tool after calling twilio__search and receiving results. Pass multiple ids to batch-fetch related operations in one call.

tools.name: twilio-docs__twilio__retrieve
tools.risk_rationale: Upstream advertises readOnlyHint=true and destructiveHint=false. The tool only fetches static documentation/schema detail for ids already returned by twilio__search (e.g. 'op::{api}::{operation_id}'); it does not itself call any Twilio API operation, send any message, or alter any resource, so it carries no external-communication or mutating effect of its own.

tools.description: Use natural language queries with Wolfram|Alpha to get up-to-date computational results about entities in chemistry, physics, geography, history, art, astronomy, and more.
tools.name: wolframalpha__WolframAlpha
tools.risk_rationale: Upstream advertises readOnlyHint=true, destructiveHint=false and openWorldHint=false. This is a single-field natural-language query into Wolfram|Alpha's computational knowledge engine, functionally equivalent to a search/calculator lookup; the description and schema expose no write, send, or external-account effect.

tools.description:
Uses semantic search to retrieve any relevant information from Wolfram.
Always use this tool at the start of new conversations or if the topic changes to ensure you have up-to-date relevant information.
This uses semantic search, so the context argument should be written in natural language (not a search query) and contain as much detail as possible (up to 250 words).

context.description: A detailed summary of what the user is trying to achieve or learn about.

tools.name: wolframalpha__WolframContext
tools.risk_rationale: Upstream advertises readOnlyHint=true, destructiveHint=false and openWorldHint=false. The tool performs a semantic-search retrieval over Wolfram's own information store given a free-text context description; it has a single input field and no parameters capable of writing, sending, or altering any resource.

tools.description:
Evaluates Wolfram Language code for the user in a Wolfram Language kernel.
If a formatted result is provided as a markdown link, use that in your response instead of typing out the output.
Parse natural language input with `\[FreeformPrompt]["query"]`, which is analogous to ctrl+= input in notebooks.
Natural language input is parsed before evaluation, so it works like macro expansion.
You should ALWAYS use this natural language input to obtain things like `Quantity`, `DateObject`, `Entity`, etc.
This is a stateless kernel, so you cannot reuse definitions from previous evaluations.

code.description: The Wolfram Language code to evaluate.

timeConstraint.description: The time constraint for the evaluation (default is 60 seconds).

tools.name: wolframalpha__WolframLanguageEvaluator
tools.risk_rationale: Upstream sets readOnlyHint=true, and the description confirms a stateless Wolfram Language kernel with no file, network or account access across calls -- a compute sandbox, not an infrastructure executor. Unlike cloudflare__execute (full CRUD against a real cloud API) or framer__exec (mutates a real SaaS project), nothing this tool runs can reach outside its own ephemeral evaluation.
